thread:
ara: Heads-up — we've got SCIM failures after we switched the OIDC client during the SSO cutover. Symptoms: SCIM provisioner can't decrypt stored tokens and IdP rejects some assertion audiences. Seeing mixed errors: KMS Decrypt fails for some token blobs but succeeds for others. Logs: 
```
2026-06-10T14:34:02Z scim-provisioner error="KMSDecryptFailed: InvalidCiphertextException" token_id=tok-7f2a user=marie@example.com
2026-06-10T14:34:03Z scim-provisioner http 403 POST /Users -> {"error":"forbidden"}
2026-06-10T14:35:10Z idp error="invalid_audience" client_id=old-client-123 assertion_id=asp-994
```
This looks like a partial migration: some tokens were encrypted with a newly created CMK (alias/scim-provisioner) in the staging account that got aliased to the same alias in prod during the rollout, causing mismatched key ARNs. @naveen can you confirm recent alias/key activity?

naveen: looking. There was an automation step to create a new key for the OIDC client handshake, and a later job copied aliases across accounts for cleanup. I see CreateKey pk-0a1b2c at 2026-06-10T14:30:45Z and a subsequent CreateAlias that pointed alias/scim-provisioner -> key-id pk-0a1b2c in prod at 14:31:02Z. But older tokens were encrypted with pk-9f8e7d; that key still exists but the alias was moved. CloudTrail shows DeleteAlias for alias/scim-provisioner at 14:31:01Z followed by CreateAlias->pk-0a1b2c at 14:31:02Z. So alias reuse caused different CMKs to own the alias over time. That would definitely break decrypts for older ciphertexts.

lia-security: alias reuse is a dangerous pattern. KMS ciphertext includes the keyId, but our token storage flow resolves alias at encrypt time and then stores ciphertext without keyId metadata. That was a design shortcut. If alias was repointed we lose the mapping. Confirm whether token records include key fingerprint. If not, we must treat this as root cause. Also check if any PutKeyPolicy or ReEncrypt events happened.

ara: confirmed — token metadata only stores cipher blob and token_id, no key-id. We rely on alias existing. Yikes. For immediate mitigation I'm pausing the alias-change job and re-creating the original alias pointing to the old key so the provisioner can decrypt existing tokens. Can we avoid data loss by restoring alias->pk-9f8e7d?

naveen: I can re-create alias -> pk-9f8e7d if the key still exists and hasn't been scheduled for deletion. Quick check: aws kms list-keys shows pk-9f8e7d present and key state = Enabled. I'll re-create alias/scim-provisioner-old pointing to pk-9f8e7d and update the provisioner to try that alias as fallback. Patch to provisioner config: add env SCIM_KMS_ALIASES=alias/scim-provisioner,alias/scim-provisioner-old.

ops-lead: mitigation steps agreed: 1) pause alias replication job (done by infra-automation), 2) reattach alias/scim-provisioner-old to old key and add fallback alias to provisioner config, 3) restore any deleted aliases if possible, 4) add a one-time re-encrypt path for tokens that must be moved to new key, 5) treat alias reuse as vuln/availability hazard in vuln triage. @naveen please apply 2 and 3. @lia-security we need policy changes to prevent alias deletion without a ticket for keys with active ciphertexts.

infra-automation: [ACTION] alias-replicator disabled at 2026-06-10T14:38:12Z by infra-automation pending manual review.

naveen: created alias/scim-provisioner-old -> pk-9f8e7d and patched deployment to use SCIM_KMS_ALIASES. Restarting scim-provisioner.

ara: after restart I'm seeing some decrypts succeed and token flow resumes for older users. New tokens are being encrypted with the new key (pk-0a1b2c) using alias/scim-provisioner. We'll need to re-encrypt old tokens to the new key on a rolling basis. Sample log after patch: 
```
2026-06-10T14:41:22Z scim-provisioner http 200 PATCH /Users/342 user=marie@example.com action=update
```
But there are still a handful of tokens that fail because they were encrypted with a key that was actually scheduled for rotation and temporarily disabled during the copy. We're running a reconciliation job to list failed decrypt token_ids and re-encrypt after manual review.

lia-security: action items for post-incident: - never reuse aliases across keys, require alias creation with unique suffixes (alias/scim-provisioner-v{uuid}) - include explicit key-id in token metadata at encrypt time (schema change) so decrypt does not rely on alias resolution - add a KMS alias deletion alert that pages security when alias for production keys is deleted - add migration tool to re-encrypt tokens safely and track key history - add infra-automation PR gating when alias changes are proposed. Classify as high risk in vuln board.

ops-lead: agree. Add owners: @naveen implement fallback alias and re-encrypt tooling, @ara + @ops-lead run reconciliation and confirm no users remain deprovisioned, @lia-security own policy/enforcement. Postmortem draft assigned to naveen. ETA EOD.

sre-bot: [INCIDENT] service=scim-provisioner incident=INC-2026-0610-07 status=mitigated mitigated_by=naveen mitigated_at=2026-06-10T14:45:32Z runbook=https://redwood.runbooks/internal/scim-provisioning-triage :white_check_mark: 

ara: closing note — this is a good catch. Our token format design decision to omit key-id sped development but created a latent availability vuln. We'll prioritize the schema change. Thanks all. (reactions: :thumbsup: from naveen, :eyes: from lia-security)
